 Judgment

The Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101723 of 2020 is preferred by the claimants in MVC No.1885 of 2016 and the Miscellaneous First Appeal No.101722 of 2020 is preferred by the claimants in MVC No.1884 of 2016 against the common judgment and award dated 16th August, 2019 passed in MVCs No.1884 of 2016 and 1885 of 2016 by the Principal Senior NC: 2023:KHC-D:9153-DB Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Athani, (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal"), seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to with their status and rank before the Tribunal.
3. On the 12th of June, 2016, a tragic incident unfolded involving Nasir and Sohel Shaikh.
They were traveling on a motorcycle to Jaysinghpur.
Nasir was operating the motorcycle while Sohel Shaikh was the pillion rider.

At around 7:15 pm, a Tipper/Dumper with license plate MH- 09/BC-5124 approached from the opposite direction, recklessly and negligently driving at a high speed and collided with the motorcycle, resulting in both riders sustaining severe injuries to crucial parts of their bodies.

Despite receiving medical treatment, both individuals succumbed to their injuries Mr.Jamal S/O Gani Mokashi vs Shri.Abhijit S/O Subhash Patil on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142134457/
3 without showing any signs of recovery.

sentences.text: The petitions detail the earnings of the deceased and the dependency and also the mental shock and agony suffered by the dependants
Based on these circumstances, compensation is being sought.
Upon the issuance of notice, respondents 1 and 2 engaged their legal counsel and submitted their contentions.
Subsequently, based on the presented statements, the Tribunal formulated relevant issues.
In order to substantiate the petitioners' claim, two witnesses were summoned and testified as PWs1 and 2.
Exhibits P1 to P11 encompassing eleven documents were marked as evidence.
While the respondents participated through their counsel and refrained from presenting oral testimony, they introduced six documents marked as Exhibits R1 to R6.

Following the presentation of arguments,
the Tribunal rendered its impugned judgment and award, granting compensation of Rs.12,12,400/-
in MVC No.1884 of 2016 and Rs.13,19,600/- in MVC No.1884 of 2016.
5. Dissatisfied with the impugned judgments and award, the appellant-claimants have lodged these appeals with the aim of seeking an enhancement in the awarded compensation.
Having heard the arguments on both side and on perusal of records, the following points would arise for our consideration in these appeals:

(1) Whether the appellant-claimants in both appeals are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
(2) What order or award?
5. Our answer to the above points are as under:
Point No.1: in the affirmative;
Point No.2: as per final order 6.We have carefully perused the impugned judgment and award and examined the material placed before this Court.
7. With regard to MVC No.1885 of 2016 which pertains to MFA No.101723 of 2020 is concerned

,
petitioners have contended that the deceased was aged 21 years and was earning Rs,15,000/- per month from centering work.
But the same is denied by the respondents.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month which is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9153-DB Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
As per guidelines issued by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority, for the accident of the year 2016, the notional income is to be taken at Rs.8,750/-.

Though it is submitted that the deceased was aged 21 years as Mr.Jamal S/O Gani Mokashi vs Shri.Abhijit S/O Subhash Patil on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142134457/
4 on the date of accident, but as per Exhibit P1-Postmortem report that the deceased was aged 26 years and hence the multiplier 17 is applicable, which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: As the deceased was a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
After deducting 50%, the monthly income comes 6,125/-.

Hence,
the loss of dependency would be Rs.12,49,500.00 (Rs.6,125/- x 12 x 17).
Accordingly same is awarded.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra),
appellants are entitled for compensation of Rs.80,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 2) towards loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- each is awarded towards funeral expenses and towards loss of estate.

Regarding MVC No.1884 which corresponds to MFA No.101722 of 2020, PW1, petitioner No.1,
provided his testimony.

He conveyed that his son Nasir was approximately 19 years old at the time of the accident and was earning Rs.15,000/- monthly as a mechanic, in addition to another Rs.15,000/- per month from milk vending.
Apart from this oral testimony, no other evidence was submitted by the petitioners to corroborate the deceased's income.
Consequently, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.

However, this assessment diverges from the guidelines set forth by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which mandates the notional income for accidents in the year 2016 to be Rs.8,750/-.
9.
Furthermore, as per the ruling of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in. PRANAY SETHI supra ,40% of the income should be factored in for future prospects.
Considering the deceased's bachelor status, a deduction of 50% towards personal expenses is applied.
Following this adjustment, the monthly income amounts to Rs.6,125/-.
Consequently, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9153-DB loss of dependency is calculated at Rs.13,23,000.00 (Rs.6,125/- x 12 x 18) and is awarded accordingly.

Referring again to the Hon'ble Supreme Court's decision in PRANAY SETHI (supra), the appellants are deemed eligible for compensation which includes Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3) for loss of consortium, as well as Rs.15,000/- each for funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
